questions.question: The management function responsible for recruiting, training, compensating, and supporting employees is
questions.explanation: Human resources management. Human resources management makes sure an organization has the right people with the right skills and that employees are treated fairly and legally. Financial management handles money and investments, operations management oversees production and daily activities, and marketing management directs efforts to reach customers. Every department depends on human resources to find and develop its employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of human resources management

questions.question: A customer calls a store and asks the employee to read back the full credit-card number on file to confirm it is correct. What should the employee do?

options.A: Write the number down for the customer's next visit
options.B: Email the full number to the customer
options.D: Verify only the last four digits according to store policy

questions.explanation: Verify only the last four digits according to store policy. Most businesses limit how much payment information employees can see or share, often showing only the last four digits, because full card numbers can be overheard, intercepted, or stolen. Reading the number aloud, emailing it, or writing it down all expose sensitive data unnecessarily. Following data-protection policies protects customers and keeps the business compliant with payment-security standards.

performanceIndicator.text: Comply with strategies to protect digital customer data (e.g., information about customers, customers' credit-card numbers, passwords, customer transactions)

questions.question: Halvorsen Engineering has a library of past project reports, but new project teams rarely use it and keep repeating the same mistakes. Which step of the knowledge-management process is the company failing to complete?

options.B: Storing knowledge in a central location

questions.explanation: Applying knowledge to new work. The company has already captured and stored knowledge in its library, but the value of knowledge management comes from using it to improve decisions and work. Making the library easy to search and building it into project planning would help teams apply what is already known.

performanceIndicator.text: Apply knowledge management processes

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a manager directing employees:

options.A: Creating a new department and assigning its staff
options.B: Setting next year's sales goals for the region
options.C: Comparing monthly sales results with the budget
options.D: Coaching the team as it learns a new procedure

questions.explanation: Coaching the team as it learns a new procedure. Directing involves guiding, communicating with, and motivating employees as they carry out their work, which is what explaining a procedure and encouraging the team does. Setting goals is planning, comparing sales with the budget is controlling, and creating a new department is organizing.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss managerial considerations in directing

questions.question: An insurance adjuster is reviewing a storm-damage claim from a small business owner. The adjuster's manager suggests underestimating the damage to keep the company's payout low, even though the policy clearly covers the full loss. What should the adjuster do?

options.B: Ask the owner to accept less in exchange for a future discount
options.D: Assess the damage accurately and pay what the policy covers

questions.explanation: Assess the damage accurately and pay what the policy covers. Insurance customers pay premiums expecting fair treatment when they have a covered loss. Deliberately underestimating a valid claim is unethical and may be illegal. Following the suggestion, denying the claim, or pressuring the owner to accept less all put the company's short-term savings ahead of its obligation to the customer.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in risk management

questions.question: Which of the following is a common constraint that project managers must balance:
questions.explanation: Time, cost, and scope. Project managers work within limits on how much time, money, and work (scope) a project involves. Changing one usually affects the others; for example, adding features increases cost or time. Price, product, and place are elements of the marketing mix, and supply, demand, and equilibrium are economic concepts.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of project management

questions.question: A temporary effort undertaken to create a unique result is a
questions.explanation: Project. A project has a defined beginning and end and produces something specific, such as a new website or a store opening. A process is a repeated series of activities, a policy is a general guideline for decisions, and a procedure is a set of steps for routine work.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of project management

questions.question: A small business's computers slow down whenever employees open several large files at once. Which hardware upgrade would most likely improve performance?
questions.explanation: Adding more memory (RAM). RAM is the temporary memory a computer uses to run programs and work with open files, so more RAM lets it handle several large files without slowing down. A larger monitor improves the viewing area but not processing speed. A new keyboard affects typing, and a desktop background has no effect on performance.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss principles of computer systems

questions.question: Which of the following is an ethical issue in business operations:

options.B: Ordering supplies from a new vendor
options.C: Choosing a new layout for the warehouse

questions.explanation: Falsifying safety inspection records. Falsifying safety records is dishonest, could endanger workers and customers, and may violate laws, which makes it a serious ethical problem. Choosing paint colors, scheduling deliveries, and ordering from a new vendor are ordinary operational decisions that don't involve right and wrong, unless something unfair or dishonest is done in the process.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in operations

questions.question: A feature of project-management software that automatically shifts the dates of later tasks when an earlier task is delayed is called
questions.explanation: Task dependency linking. When tasks are linked as dependencies, the software knows one task cannot start until another finishes, so a delay automatically pushes back everything that depends on it. Resource leveling adjusts work so no person is overbooked. Milestone tracking marks key checkpoints, and a baseline comparison shows how the current schedule differs from the original plan, but neither reschedules tasks on its own.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize project-management software

questions.question: Studying outside factors such as the economy, laws, and competitors is
questions.explanation: Environmental scanning. An environmental scan monitors external forces that could create opportunities or threats for a business. Internal auditing reviews a company's own records and controls, inventory control manages stock levels, and performance appraisal evaluates employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Conduct an environmental scan to obtain business information

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary goal of supply chain management:

options.A: Producing as many goods as possible regardless of demand
options.B: Selecting advertising media for new products
options.C: Delivering products where needed at a reasonable cost
options.D: Setting wages for employees throughout the company

questions.explanation: Delivering products where needed at a reasonable cost. Supply chain management aims to match supply with demand efficiently, getting the right products to the right places at the right time while controlling costs. Producing without regard to demand creates waste, and choosing advertising media and setting wages are marketing and human resources activities.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of supply chain management

questions.question: A bar chart that shows project tasks along a timeline is a
questions.explanation: Gantt chart. Gantt charts display tasks, their start and end dates, and their overlap, making it easy to track the project schedule. Pie charts show parts of a whole, fishbone diagrams help identify causes of problems, and SWOT analysis is a strategic planning tool.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage project schedule

questions.question: Henley Manufacturing's purchasing agent must buy steel for the next quarter. Supplier A offers the lowest price but has delivered late four times this year. Supplier B charges 3% more but has never missed a delivery. Which of the following factors should the agent consider in addition to price:

options.A: Supplier reliability and its effect on production schedules
options.B: Which supplier's office is closer to the agent's home
options.C: The color of each supplier's logo

questions.explanation: Supplier reliability and its effect on production schedules. A late steel delivery can stop production, idle workers, and delay customer orders, so a supplier's reliability can be worth more than a small price difference. Good purchasing decisions weigh price together with quality, service, and dependability. A supplier's logo and gifts have no effect on business performance, and the agent's personal convenience shouldn't influence a decision made on behalf of the company.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing

questions.question: Which of the following would a business examine as part of an environmental scan:

options.A: Its policy on internal email and file sharing
options.B: The office supply orders placed last quarter
options.C: Its employee break schedule for the next month
options.D: A proposed increase in the state minimum wage

questions.explanation: A proposed increase in the state minimum wage. Environmental scans focus on external factors, and a change in minimum-wage law could significantly affect labor costs. Break schedules, supply orders, and email policies are internal matters that the business controls directly.

performanceIndicator.text: Conduct an environmental scan to obtain business information

questions.question: Which of the following is a resource that should be identified when planning a project:

options.D: The people, equipment, and money needed

questions.explanation: The people, equipment, and money needed. Identifying resources such as staff, equipment, materials, time, and budget helps a project manager determine what is needed, when, and at what cost, which prevents delays and overspending. A mission statement guides the whole company but doesn't list what a specific project needs. The stock price and last year's satisfaction scores describe the company, not the resources required to complete the project's work.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify resources needed for project

questions.question: Information that comes from a recognized expert and cites evidence is considered
questions.explanation: Credible. Credible information comes from qualified, identifiable sources and is supported by evidence others can check. Biased information favors one side, outdated information may no longer be accurate, and anonymous information can't be checked for expertise or motives. Businesses rely on credible sources when making important decisions.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: During the litigation process, the stage in which each side exchanges documents and takes sworn statements from witnesses is called
questions.explanation: Discovery. Discovery lets both parties learn the facts and evidence before trial through requests for documents, written questions, and depositions. Pleadings are the initial filings, such as the complaint and answer, that start the case. An appeal asks a higher court to review a decision after trial, and the judgment is the court's final decision. Discovery often encourages settlement because both sides see the strength of the evidence.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the litigation process

questions.question: Why do businesses keep an audit trail of changes made to customer records?

options.A: To show who changed records and when
options.B: To replace the need for regular data backups
options.C: To allow any employee to edit any customer record
options.D: To make the database run faster for users

questions.explanation: To show who changed records and when. An audit trail records each change, the user who made it, and the time, which helps identify mistakes, detect unauthorized changes, and restore accurate information. It doesn't speed up the database, it complements rather than replaces backups, and it supports access controls instead of opening records to everyone. Audit trails are also required in many regulated industries.

performanceIndicator.text: Adhere to data change best practices

questions.question: Making small, ongoing improvements to processes rather than one major change is the concept of
questions.explanation: Kaizen. Kaizen is a Japanese term for continuous improvement through many small changes, often suggested by employees who do the work. Reengineering is a radical redesign of a process, outsourcing hires another company to do work, and benchmarking compares a business's practices with those of industry leaders.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the need for continuous improvement of the quality process

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason a business might organize itself into divisions based on geographic regions:

options.A: Customer needs differ from one region to another
options.B: It wants every decision made at headquarters
options.C: It sells only one product to one type of customer
options.D: All of its products are made in a single factory

questions.explanation: Customer needs differ from one region to another. Geographic divisions let a business tailor products, pricing, and service to regional differences in customer needs and conditions. A single factory, highly centralized decision making, and a single product for one type of customer are all situations in which geographic divisions would add little value.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain managerial considerations in organizing

questions.question: Knowledge that is easy to write down and share, such as a written procedure, is
questions.explanation: Explicit. Explicit knowledge can be put into words, recorded, and passed along in documents, databases, and manuals. Tacit knowledge is based on personal experience and is hard to express. Implicit knowledge could be written down but hasn't been yet, and embedded knowledge is built into an organization's routines, products, or culture rather than recorded on its own.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of knowledge management

questions.question: Two siblings want to open a coffee roastery together. They want to share decision making and profits, but they don't want their personal savings to be at risk if the business fails, and they prefer simpler paperwork than a corporation requires. Which form of ownership best meets their needs?
questions.explanation: Limited liability company. An LLC protects owners' personal assets while offering more flexible management and less paperwork than a corporation. A general partnership exposes both partners to unlimited personal liability, a sole proprietorship has only one owner, and a cooperative is owned and controlled by members who use its services, which doesn't fit two siblings running a business.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of business ownership

questions.question: Comparing a project's actual progress to the plan is part of
questions.explanation: Monitoring and controlling. During monitoring and controlling, the project manager tracks progress, compares it with the baseline plan, and takes action to correct any gaps. Initiating authorizes the project, closing wraps it up, and defining scope happens during planning when the team decides what work is included.

performanceIndicator.text: Execute and control projects

questions.question: Before the busy holiday season, an electronics retailer purposely builds up extra stock of gaming consoles to meet the expected rise in demand. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Anticipation inventory. Anticipation inventory is built ahead of a predictable increase in demand, such as a holiday season. Safety stock protects against unexpected demand or supply delays, dead stock is merchandise that no longer sells, and pipeline inventory is stock that is in transit between locations.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss types of inventory

questions.question: Which of the following is a way technology has changed how businesses serve customers:

options.A: Customers have fewer ways to contact businesses
options.B: Businesses no longer need any customer service staff
options.C: Customers can get help at any hour through chat
options.D: Customers must visit stores in person for most help

questions.explanation: Customers can get help at any hour through chat. Chat, help centers, and apps let customers get answers anytime, which improves convenience and lowers costs for businesses. Technology has expanded rather than reduced the ways customers can reach businesses, and most companies still need people to handle complex problems.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify ways that technology impacts business

questions.question: Tasks that are both urgent and important should usually be done
questions.explanation: First. Prioritizing by urgency and importance ensures that critical, time-sensitive work gets done before less important tasks. Leaving it until last or doing it only if time allows risks missed deadlines with serious consequences, and handing it off by default avoids responsibility. Important tasks that aren't urgent should be scheduled, and unimportant tasks can often be delegated or dropped.

performanceIndicator.text: Organize and prioritize work

questions.question: Following not only the exact words of a law but also its purpose is complying with the law's
questions.explanation: Spirit and intent. Complying with the spirit and intent means understanding why a law exists, such as protecting consumers or workers, and behaving in ways that support that goal. Loopholes are gaps that let people avoid a law's purpose while technically obeying it. Penalties are consequences for breaking a law, and the appeal process allows decisions to be challenged in court.

performanceIndicator.text: Comply with the spirit and intent of laws and regulations

questions.question: When two project team members disagree about how to complete a task, the project manager should first

options.B: remove one member from the project.

questions.explanation: Understand each person's position. Understanding both viewpoints helps the manager find the real cause of the disagreement and a solution both can support. Deciding without discussion may leave one member resentful, removing someone is an extreme step for an ordinary disagreement, and ignoring conflict often lets it grow and hurt the team's work.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage project team

questions.question: Which word-processing feature automatically checks a document for misspelled words:
questions.explanation: Spell check. Spell check identifies words that may be misspelled and suggests corrections, though writers should still proofread because it may miss correctly spelled words used incorrectly. Mail merge combines a document with a list of names and addresses, track changes records edits, and page layout controls margins and orientation.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic word processing skills

questions.question: The first step in assessing information needs is to

options.A: collect as much data as possible.
options.B: determine what decision it will support.

questions.explanation: Determine what decision it will support. Knowing what decision must be made shows what information is relevant, which prevents wasted time gathering data that won't help. Collecting as much data as possible without a purpose can overwhelm decision makers. New software may help later but doesn't identify what information is needed, and a final report comes only after information has been gathered and analyzed.

performanceIndicator.text: Assess information needs

questions.question: Key checkpoints that mark the completion of major phases in a project plan are
questions.explanation: Milestones. Milestones are significant events in a project, such as finishing the design phase, that help the team and stakeholders track progress. Work packages are the smallest units of work in a WBS, stakeholders are people affected by the project, and constraints are limits such as time, cost, and scope.

performanceIndicator.text: Plan project

questions.question: Viewing work as a series of connected steps that cross departments is
questions.explanation: Business process thinking. Business process thinking looks at how work flows from start to finish across the organization, rather than focusing on each department separately. This view reveals delays and handoff problems that department-only thinking misses. Budgeting, vertical integration, and segmentation are unrelated business concepts.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss business process thinking and its impact

questions.question: The management function of recruiting, hiring, and training employees is
questions.explanation: Staffing. Staffing focuses on getting the right people into the right jobs and developing them. Directing involves guiding and motivating employees once they are in place, controlling compares performance with standards, and planning sets goals. Some businesses treat staffing as part of organizing, but it is still distinct from these other functions.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe managerial considerations in staffing

questions.question: Ellison is creating a plan for his school's charity fun run. He has listed every task and estimated how long each will take. What should he do next to build a realistic schedule?

options.A: Choose a theme and design for the event T-shirts
options.B: Identify which tasks depend on others
options.C: Start selling tickets so the team can track demand
options.D: Announce the event date to the school immediately

questions.explanation: Identify which tasks depend on others. Understanding task dependencies, such as needing a permit before marketing the route, shows the order work must happen in and how long the whole project will take. Choosing T-shirt themes, announcing a date, or selling tickets before the schedule is built could lead to commitments the team can't meet.

performanceIndicator.text: Develop project plan

questions.question: A written agreement in which a customer accepts the known risks of an activity and agrees not to sue for ordinary injuries is a
questions.explanation: Liability waiver. Businesses such as gyms and adventure parks use liability waivers to inform customers of risks and limit legal claims. Waivers usually do not protect against gross negligence. A warranty is a promise about a product's quality, an indemnity bond guarantees payment for certain losses, and a nondisclosure agreement protects confidential information.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss legal considerations affecting risk management

questions.question: Which of the following internal records would help a manager identify the store's best-selling products:
questions.explanation: Sales records. Sales records show which products were sold, in what quantities, and when, allowing managers to identify best-sellers and plan inventory and promotions. Time cards track employee hours, the lease describes the terms for renting the building, and an insurance policy describes coverage against losses. None of those records track product sales.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor internal records for business information

questions.question: Henrik's team has just finished installing a new inventory system for a warehouse client. The client has tested the system and signed a form stating that it meets all agreed requirements. In which project phase is Henrik's team?
questions.explanation: Closing. Formal client acceptance of the deliverables is a key closing activity, along with releasing resources and capturing lessons learned. Initiating authorizes the project, planning defines how the work will be done, and executing is when the team builds the deliverables before they are tested and accepted.

performanceIndicator.text: Close project

questions.question: Akosua is preparing a five-minute presentation for her company's leadership team about quarterly sales results. Her draft has 22 slides, each with several paragraphs of text. Which change would most improve her presentation?

options.A: Use fewer slides and show key results in charts
options.B: Add more text to each slide so nothing is missed
options.C: Use a smaller font to fit more information
options.D: Use a different color scheme on each slide

questions.explanation: Use fewer slides and show key results in charts. Fewer slides fit the short time limit, and charts let leaders see sales results quickly, while Akosua explains the details aloud. Adding more text or shrinking the font would make slides harder to read and overwhelm the audience. Changing colors on every slide would look inconsistent and distract from the information without making it any clearer.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic presentation applications

questions.question: While reviewing monthly reports, the manager of Brookside Market notices that inventory records show 200 cases of bottled water in stock, but a physical count finds only 140 cases. What should the manager do?

options.A: Investigate the cause of the difference
options.B: Correct the records to match the count and move on
options.C: Ignore the difference because the numbers are close

questions.explanation: Investigate the cause of the difference. Monitoring internal records helps managers spot problems early, and a 60-case gap suggests theft, damage, or errors that should be investigated and corrected. Ignoring it allows the problem to continue. Simply changing the records hides the loss without finding out why it happened, so it may keep occurring. Ordering more stock without finding the cause could lead to overstocking or repeat losses.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor internal records for business information

questions.question: A business owned by one person who is personally responsible for all of its debts is a
questions.explanation: Sole proprietorship. A sole proprietorship is the simplest form of ownership: the owner keeps all profits but has unlimited personal liability for business debts. Corporations and limited liability companies protect owners' personal assets, and a limited partnership has at least one general partner and one or more limited partners.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of business ownership

questions.question: At Delmont Restaurant, food waste has increased because cooks often prepare more side dishes than customers order. The manager asks employees for ideas to reduce costs. Which suggestion would best help control this expense?

options.A: Raise menu prices without changing preparation
options.B: Prepare sides in smaller batches based on orders
options.D: Buy more ingredients in bulk at lower prices

questions.explanation: Prepare sides in smaller batches based on orders. Preparing food based on demand reduces waste and the cost of unused ingredients, directly addressing the problem. Raising prices doesn't fix the waste. Throwing away leftovers more often increases waste. Buying more in bulk could increase spoilage if the restaurant keeps overproducing.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain employee's role in expense control

questions.question: After a manager assigns a task to an employee, the manager should

options.A: assign the same task to several people without telling them.
options.B: never ask about the task again.

questions.explanation: Check progress at agreed-upon times. Monitoring delegated tasks ensures work stays on schedule and allows the manager to provide help if problems arise. Never checking in may cause missed deadlines. Doing the task himself/herself defeats the purpose of delegating, and assigning the same task to several people secretly wastes time and creates confusion.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor and ensure completion of delegated tasks

questions.question: The interconnected system of suppliers, manufacturers, warehouses, and retailers that move a product to customers is a
questions.explanation: Supply chain network. A supply chain network includes all the organizations and locations involved in sourcing, making, storing, and delivering a product. The marketing mix refers to product, price, place, and promotion, the chain of command shows reporting relationships, and a product line is a group of related products.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe supply chain networks
